Upcoming Election Information

November 3, 2026 General Election

Dallas County

Dallas County residents can vote at any Dallas County Vote Center during Early Voting and on Election Day. The polling location for the City of Coppell will be located in the meeting rooms of the Cozby Library and Community Commons, 177 North Heartz Road, Coppell.

Information regarding additional Early Voting and Election Day Polling Locations is available on the Dallas County Election Administration website.

Dallas County Early Voting Dates and Times:

DatesDay of the WeekTimes
October 19 - 24, 2026Monday - Saturday7:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m.
October 25, 2026Sunday12:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m.
October 26 - 30, 2026Monday - Friday7:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m.


Denton County

Please note that the Coppell Greens subdivision and The Villas at Lake Vista subdivision are located in Denton County. 

For Early Voting, Denton County residents can vote anywhere in Denton County. Information regarding Early Voting polling locations is available on the Denton County Election Administration website.

Denton County Early Voting Dates and Times:

DatesDay of the WeekTimes
October 19 - 23, 2026  Monday - Friday8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.
October 24, 2026Saturday7:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m.
October 25, 2026Sunday11:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.
October 26 - 30, 2026Monday - Friday7:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m.

On Election Day, Denton County residents must vote within their precinct.

Important Dates:

Last Day to Register to Vote is Monday, October 5, 2026.

First Day of Early Voting by Personal Appearance is Monday, October 19, 2026.

Last Day to Apply for Ballot by Mail (received, not postmarked) is Friday, October 23, 2026. 

City of Coppell Election Postings and Notices:


Candidate Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible to run for City Councilmember in Places Two, Four, Six and Mayor, the following eligibility requirements must be met:

  • Be a United State citizen.
  • Be a registered voter of the City at the time of filing for office.
  • Be 18 years of age or older on or before the first day of the term in which they are elected.
  • Have not been determined mentally incompetent by a final judgment of a court.
  • Have not been finally convicted of a felony from which the person has not been pardoned or otherwise released from the resulting disabilities.
  • Have resided continuously in Texas on or before one year preceding the filing deadline.
  • Shall have resided, for at least twelve (12) months next preceding the date of the election, within the corporate limits of the city, or within territory annexed into the city prior to the filing deadline.
  • Shall not, after notice of any delinquency, be in arrears in the payment of any taxes or other liabilities due the city. "In arrears" is defined herein to mean that payment has not been received within ninety (90) days from due date and has not been protested under the same provisions as provided for in the Coppell City Charter.
  • No candidate may file in a single election for more than one (1) office or place position as provided by the Coppell City Charter.
  • An incumbent city councilmember seeking re-election must file for the same place position number currently being served.
  • No employee of the City of Coppell shall continue in such position after filing for an elective office provided for in the Coppell City Charter.
